verdict.rationale: Vercel's docs say developers can build against official SDKs in two ways: point the existing OpenAI or Anthropic client libraries at the gateway with a base-URL swap, or use Vercel's own AI SDK, shown with a ToolLoopAgent code example. Depth beyond that is undocumented: there is no dedicated gateway SDK reference, no language or package matrix, and no hands-on corroboration, so coverage is partial rather than complete. missing for 10: a documented first-party gateway SDK reference with supported languages and packages, SDK feature-parity details for gateway options beyond the providerOptions snippets, independent or hands-on corroboration of SDK usage

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Point your existing OpenAI or Anthropic SDK at AI Gateway. Same calls, no rewrites.
You can use the AI Gateway's Chat Completions API with existing tools and libraries like the OpenAI client libraries and AI SDK.
Move existing OpenAI, Anthropic, and AI SDK integrations to AI Gateway with a base URL swap.
You can use existing OpenAI client libraries, switch to AI Gateway with a URL change, and keep your current tools and workflows without code rewrites.
